logp.method_description: The log P of the rhenium complexes was determined using the shake flask method, as described previously.[46,83] An orbital shaker was used to shake a known amount of each complex (ReL1-ReL6) suspended in water (pre-saturated with n-Octanol) for 48 hours. The solution was centrifuged for 10 minutes at 3000 rpm to allow phase separation. Different ratios (v/v, 0.5:1, 1:1, and 2:1) of the saturated solutions were shaken with pre-saturated n-Octanol for 20 minutes on an orbital shaker to get the partition coefficient. The quantity of ruthenium in saturated aqueous solution was then determined by ICP-MS.

A hydrophobicity test was performed for the synthesized complexes employing the “shake-flask” method and octanol–water phase partition coefficient. The complex was dissolved in a mixture of water and octanol, followed by shaking for 24 h. Then, the mixture was allowed to settle for 30 min or centrifuged at 5000 rpm for 20 min. The resulting two phases were collected separately without cross-contamination of one solvent layer into the other. The concentration of the complex in each phase was determined by UV-visible absorption spectroscopy at room temperature. The presented results are the mean values obtained from three independent experiments. The sample solution concentration was used to calculate log Po/w.
